question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{\sqrt{x}-1}{x-1} & =\frac{\sqrt{1}-1}{1-1}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the numerator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the numerator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{\sqrt{x}-1}{x-1} & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{(\sqrt{x}-1)(\sqrt{x}+1)}{(x-1)(\sqrt{x}+1)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{(\sqrt{x})}^{2}-{1}^{2}}{(x-1)(\sqrt{x}+1)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{x-1}{(x-1)(\sqrt{x}+1)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{\cancel{x-1}}{\cancel{(x-1)}(\sqrt{x}+1)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}+1} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1}+1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
